def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers_set = set(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    # Keep deterministic: no randomness

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for node in route:
            s += demands[node]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for a, b in zip(route, route[1:]):
            c += matrix[a][b]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    # Initial incumbent construction (edit 1): Clarke-Wright savings with deterministic merges
    # Creates feasible routes first, then local search refines.
    cust_list = sorted(customers_set)

    loads = [demands[c] for c in cust_list]
    rid_of = {c: idx for idx, c in enumerate(cust_list)}
    # For each route, allow at most one merge direction by using ends; we keep routes directed lists.

    # Deterministic savings list
    savings = []
    for a_i in range(len(cust_list)):
        a = cust_list[a_i]
        da = matrix[depot][a]
        for b_j in range(a_i + 1, len(cust_list)):
            b = cust_list[b_j]
            db = matrix[depot][b]
            sav = da + db - matrix[a][b]
            # tie-break by (a,b)
            savings.append((sav, a, b))
    savings.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))

    active = [True] * len(routes)

    def merge_routes(i, j, orientation):
        # orientation:
        # 0: routes[i] + routes[j]  (i tail to j head) => append j to i
        # 1: routes[i] + reverse(routes[j]) (i tail to j tail) => reverse j then append
        # 2: reverse(routes[i]) + routes[j] (i head to j head) => reverse i then append
        # 3: reverse(routes[i]) + reverse(routes[j]) (i head to j tail) => reverse both then append
        nonlocal routes, loads, rid_of, active
        if not active[i] or not active[j]:
            return False
        li = loads[i]
        lj = loads[j]
        if li + lj > capacity:
            return False

        ri = routes[i]
        rj = routes[j]
        if orientation == 0:
            newr = ri + rj
        elif orientation == 1:
            newr = ri + rj[::-1]
        elif orientation == 2:
            newr = ri[::-1] + rj
        else:
            newr = ri[::-1] + rj[::-1]

        # Apply
        routes[i] = newr
        loads[i] = li + lj
        active[j] = False
        routes[j] = []
        # Update mapping for moved customers
        for x in newr:
            rid_of[x] = i
        return True

    # Greedy savings merges, best-first
    for _, a, b in savings:
        if a not in rid_of or b not in rid_of:
            continue
        ra = rid_of[a]
        rb = rid_of[b]
        if ra == rb or not active[ra] or not active[rb]:
            continue
        # Allow merges based on ends; deterministic checks
        # Case: tail(a_route)=a and head(b_route)=b => orientation 0
        # Also try other end combinations by orientation.
        # We only allow each merge to be a simple end-to-end concatenation.
        a_route = routes[ra]
        b_route = routes[rb]
        if not a_route or not b_route:
            continue
        tail_a = a_route[-1]
        head_a = a_route[0]
        tail_b = b_route[-1]
        head_b = b_route[0]

        # Choose first feasible orientation in a deterministic order for stability
        # Prefer the orientation that actually reflects the savings arc a->b
        merged = False
        if tail_a == a and head_b == b:
            merged = merge_routes(ra, rb, 0)
        if not merged and tail_a == a and tail_b == b:
            # a tail -> b tail means reverse b
            merged = merge_routes(ra, rb, 1)
        if not merged and head_a == a and head_b == b:
            # a head -> b head means reverse a
            merged = merge_routes(ra, rb, 2)
        if not merged and head_a == a and tail_b == b:

            merged = merge_routes(ra, rb, 3)

        for x in r:
            present.add(x)

        for c in missing:
            routes.append([c])

        # returns (best_pos, best_delta_cost) relative to current route cost

                best_pos = pos
        return best_pos, best_delta

    def apply_insertion(route, pos, node):
        route.insert(pos, node)

    def apply_removal(route, k):
        del route[k]

    def route_remove_cost_delta(ri, k):
        # delta in ri cost if node ri[k] removed from ri
        n = len(ri)
        node = ri[k]
        if n == 1:
            return -route_cost(ri)
        if k == 0:
            prev = depot
            nxt = ri[1]
            old = matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]
            new = matrix[prev][nxt]
            return new - old
        if k == n - 1:
            prev = ri[n - 2]
            nxt = depot
            old = matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]
            new = matrix[prev][nxt]
            return new - old
        prev = ri[k - 1]
        nxt = ri[k + 1]
        old = matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]
        new = matrix[prev][nxt]
        return new - old

    base_total = total_cost(routes)

    max_outer = 3
    for _ in range(max_outer):
        improved = False
        for i in range(len(routes)):
            ri = routes[i]
            if not ri:
                continue
            for k in range(len(ri)):
                node = ri[k]
                new_load_i = loads[i] - demands[node]
                if new_load_i < 0:
                    continue
                delta_remove_i = route_remove_cost_delta(ri, k)

                best = None  # (delta_total, j, pos)
                for j in range(len(routes)):
                    if j == i:
                        continue
                    if loads[j] + demands[node] > capacity:
                        continue
                    pos, delta_insert_j = best_insertion_cost(routes[j], node)
                    delta_total = delta_remove_i + delta_insert_j
                    if best is None or delta_total < best[0] - 1e-12:
                        best = (delta_total, j, pos)
                if best is None:
                    continue
                delta_total, j, pos = best
                if delta_total < -1e-12:
                    # apply mutation
                    apply_removal(ri, k)
                    loads[i] = new_load_i
                    apply_insertion(routes[j], pos, node)

                    base_total += delta_total
                    improved = True

            if improved:

        for i in range(nr):

                break
            ri = routes[i]
